Performance Threshold (Optional)

What is Performance Threshold?

Set the maximum acceptable reboot time in seconds. If the actual reboot time exceeds this value, device logs will automatically be collected for diagnostics and performance analysis.

📌 Default: 120 seconds | Range: 1-600 seconds

Examples

  • 120 seconds - Standard reboot target (typical: 70-85s)
  • 150 seconds - Lenient threshold for slow boots
  • 90 seconds - Strict performance requirement

Auto-Collection Behavior

  • If reboot time ≤ threshold: No logs collected (normal pass)
  • If reboot time > threshold: Logs auto-collected (when auto-collect is enabled)
  • Logs saved to: /media/apps/

Welcome to the Dashboard

Here's a quick guide to help you get started with the RDK-E Middleware QA Testing Dashboard

Column 1: Available Test Methods

This section contains all the testing methods available for your device:

  • Reboot Tests: Device reboot and performance monitoring
  • Power Management: Deep sleep, power key, and state queries
  • Screen Validation: Screenshot capture and validation
  • Input/Navigation: Send remote keys, voice commands, IR tests
  • System Tools: Memory capture, system commands, log collection

💡 Tip: Hover over any method to see detailed information about what it does!

Column 2: Test Execution Queue

Build and execute your test scenarios here:

  • Drag Methods: Drag methods from Column 1 to create your test sequence
  • Set Iterations: Specify how many times the test should run
  • Select Devices: Choose one or multiple devices to test
  • Run Tests: Click "Run Selected Sequence" to execute
  • View Results: Access results via the Jobs Queue or Results page

💡 Tip: Build complex test sequences by combining multiple methods!

Column 3: Results & Execution History

Track and review your test executions:

  • Live Monitoring: Watch test progress in real-time
  • Test Results: View pass/fail status for each method
  • Execution Logs: Access detailed logs for debugging
  • Screenshots: Review captured device screenshots
  • Filter by Date: Find tests by their execution date (UTC)

💡 Tip: Click on any execution to view detailed logs and results!

Quick Actions

  • Add New Device: Register a new device for testing
  • Services Menu: Access system commands and tools
  • Results: View all test results in table or card format
  • Log Patterns: Configure log detection patterns

Getting Started Tips

  1. Make sure you have registered at least one device via the "Add New Device" button
  2. Familiarize yourself with method tooltips - hover over any method card
  3. Start with a simple test (e.g., single Reboot method, 1 iteration, 1 device)
  4. Gradually build complex test scenarios by chaining multiple methods
  5. Review execution logs to debug and optimize your tests
  6. Use Screenshots for visual validation of device behavior

You can always access this guide from the main menu if needed.
